finding.claim: deleteAccount calls canDelete() but ignores the boolean result, so the authorization check is never enforced. Any caller can delete any account by id (broken access control / IDOR). The sibling closeAccount correctly uses assertCanDelete.
finding.source: Any authenticated user calling DELETE /accounts/{id} with an arbitrary account id

trace.note: deleteAccount(User u, long id) entry for DELETE /accounts/{id}; id is attacker-controlled
account looked up by attacker-supplied id
canDelete(u, a) returns boolean but result is discarded; no exception thrown
canDelete correctly computes admin || owner, but has no side effect

finding.guards_checked: canDelete (result unused); assertCanDelete is used in closeAccount (line 29) but not in deleteAccount. No other middleware or controller exists in the repo (single file). The account is also not null-checked, so a nonexistent id would NPE in canDelete at line 10, but that is minor.

verdict.guard_found: canDelete (src/AccountService.java:9-11) returns a boolean that is discarded at line 22; assertCanDelete (13-17) would throw but is only called in closeAccount (line 29). No other guard exists in the repo.
verdict.reason: At src/AccountService.java:22 the boolean from canDelete is discarded as a bare statement, so accounts.remove(id) at line 23 runs for any authenticated user, whereas closeAccount uses the throwing assertCanDelete at line 29.
